name: Grape Hyacinth
family: Asparagaceae, the asparagus family (the hyacinth group)
grown_as: William's grape hyacinth is Muscari aucheri 'Ocean Magic' (PG 46 in his spreadsheet): a short grape hyacinth with mid sky-blue spikes whose top flowers are white, and two or three broader grey-green leaves. Drawn as that.
habit: Small clumps 10 to 15 cm high: each bulb has two or three fairly broad, grey-green leaves and one upright flower stem, the spike standing a little above the leaves. ⚠️ CHECK: the height and how the leaves lie are from general knowledge of M. aucheri, not William's plants.

leaf.arrangement: Two or three leaves from the base of each bulb, arching outwards, often lying partly on the soil
leaf.outline: 8 to 15 cm long by 5 to 15 mm wide, broader than most grape hyacinths, widest towards the blunt end. ⚠️ CHECK the size
leaf.surface: Smooth and a little fleshy, with a shallow channel along the upper side

flower.form: A dense cone-shaped spike of tiny round bells, like a bunch of grapes upside down
flower.petals: Six tepals joined into a small urn-shaped bell, swollen in the middle and pinched at the mouth, with six tiny white teeth turned back round the rim
flower.colour: Mid sky-blue; the top few flowers (which are sterile) white
flower.centre: Not seen: the mouth is a tiny white-rimmed hole
flower.carried: Fifteen to thirty bells packed in an egg-shaped spike 2 to 3 cm long at the top of a bare stem, pointing down and outward

fruit: Inflated, papery capsules with three rounded flat wings, about 1 cm, green ripening to straw, along the stem; black seeds.
seedling: Not drawn. A single fine grass-like leaf.
winter: Nothing above ground until the leaves come up in late winter. ⚠️ CHECK: unlike the common M. armeniacum, M. aucheri is not known for sprawling autumn leaves.

leaf: one strap-shaped leaf, broader than a common grape hyacinth's, with a shallow groove
bloom: many small round bells packed in an egg-shaped spike
each bell pinched at the mouth with a white rim
mid sky-blue below, the top flowers white
bulb: a small round bulb 1.5 to 2 cm with pale brown papery skin
often with several small offset bulbs round it
shoots: two or three broad grey-green leaf tips coming up in late winter
the young flower spike, packed with tight buds, between them
flower: sky-blue spikes with white tops on short bare stems
two or three broad grey-green leaves per bulb, lower than the spikes
seedhead: papery three-winged pods along the stem
dormant: nothing above the soil in summer

look_alikes: Bluebell has larger bells hanging down one side of the stem. Muscari latifolium has one broad leaf and a two-tone spike. Spanish bluebell leaves are much broader. Young leaves look like grass or chives but are fleshy and grooved, and chives smell of onion.
